Null image is returned as failure; native temporary references are still released.

binding_reviews.calling_signature: poll(struct pollfd*,nfds_t,int)->int, pointer/u32/i32 arguments and i32 return; nfds_t is unsigned int in the SDK.
binding_reviews.rationale: Only descriptors0,count0 are used, so no caller buffer is observed or mutated. Positive waits split full u32 milliseconds into nonnegative i32-representable parts; no accidental -1 infinite timeout. Poll is explicitly blocks/reaches TimeHost. Zero is completed timeout; nonzero/error is retried, so interruptions do not report early completion, though repeated host errors may prevent progress and retries can oversleep.

calling_plan_assessment.CFDataCreate: Semantic allocator + shared byte descriptor expands to three native scalar lanes, not a one-byte &u8 exposure. The source explicitly opts into DarwinArm64ByteViewCalling.
calling_plan_assessment.CGImageCreate: DarwinArm64ScalarCalling independently places each tail at natural size/alignment: decode8@0, Bool1@8, intent4@12, total16. Narrow-register arguments are not involved; bitmap_info is32bits in register7. This is a source calling-policy audit, not fresh machine-code inspection.
calling_plan_assessment.TimeRead: Default three-or-fewer integer argument calling lanes agree with Darwin signatures for these actual uses. No cross-host approval is inferred.
calling_plan_assessment.new_SystemV_path: 40f9 adds SystemVByteViewCalling to posix_byte_view_calling; Darwin path still initializes darwin_arm64_entry, uses AArch64 argument/result registers and pointer/count lanes. The added SystemV path is not an authorization or runtime observation for these macOS bindings.

lifetime_and_cleanup.copy: CFDataCreate copies all supplied bytes into native-owned storage. No returned object borrows the Omega framebuffer.
lifetime_and_cleanup.provider: The factory keeps the original CFData reference through provider and image creation. The native promise includes independent provider ownership of its CFData backing; modern fetched provider documentation describes the CFData source but does not explicitly spell out its retain operation. This detail remains admitted vendor behavior, not a new source theorem or independently observed runtime result.
lifetime_and_cleanup.image: Apple image documentation explicitly states retention of provider and color space. Thus dropping the factory temporary references after creation preserves the image backing.
lifetime_and_cleanup.failure_paths: Failed CFData =>0; failed provider =>release_data then0; image attempt =>release_provider and release_data regardless of result. Returned nonzero image is caller-owned and must be released.
lifetime_and_cleanup.opaque_handles: Nonzero u64 is not a proof of a valid CF object, RGB color-space identity or balanced release ownership. Acceptance trusts the audited creator-to-user path and native promise; arbitrary forged handles are outside that justified path.

capability_assessment: These are explicit foreign-code trust relationships. Image requirements carry MacosImageData/MacosImageObjects; time requirements carry DarwinTimeRead/TimeHost, poll blocks. Empty additional reach is not proof of purity: image construction allocates native objects and raw bindings execute native code. No filesystem, network, desktop-observation or event-injection grant is added by this report. Actual runtime authority and exact final package policy remain independently required.
